content: There is no dedicated pytest/htmx assertion library worth adding for a FastAPI app; the htmx layer is an ordinary HTTP contract and httpx AsyncClient covers it. Asserts available server-side: send headers={'HX-Request':'true'} and compare the body against the non-htmx body to prove fragment vs full page; assert response.status_code==200 instead of 302 on the htmx path; assert response.headers['HX-Location'|'HX-Trigger'|'HX-Retarget'|'HX-Reswap'|'HX-Push-Url']; assert the returned fragment contains hx-swap-oob targets; assert the SAME template still emits method="post" action="/x" for the no-JS path. httpx AsyncClient defaults to follow_redirects=False, so 302-vs-fragment is directly assertable. Not assertable server-side: that htmx actually swapped, DOM state after swap, indicator/disabled-elt visuals, JS error handlers — those need a browser. Community consensus (htmx discussion #680) is that the server contract is the testable surface and browser tests are reserved for a handful of smoke paths.
